tools/syncthing.note: These are supported core downloads, not identical desktop GUI packages. OS integrations are separate projects. Do not treat a third-party phone client or the discontinued official Android wrapper as current core mobile support.

tools/taskwarrior.note: The current project page says Cygwin is no longer supported and recommends Windows Subsystem for Linux. Phone clients are separate projects and are not counted here.

tools/ventoy.note: These labels describe the host used to prepare a bootable USB, not every operating system an ISO can boot. Installing Ventoy can erase the selected drive. The page does not assert a native macOS installer.

tools/kitchenowl.note: These are clients for the KitchenOwl service.
tools/kitchenowl.details: The current release has Linux, Windows, macOS, Android and Web artifacts, and the project documents iOS.

tools/logseq.note: The 2.0.2 DB beta has desktop and Android artifacts and links a browser app; the official downloads page also offers an iOS app on the App Store. The DB version's own iOS app is in TestFlight review per the release notes, so it is not the App Store listing recorded here. File-graph 0.10.x and DB graphs are different workflows; do not assume interchangeable data or sync.

tools/silverbullet.note: This listing is scoped to the open-source MIT SilverBullet Server and its browser/PWA interface.
tools/silverbullet.details: SilverBullet Desktop is explicitly not open source according to the project FAQ and is excluded from native Linux/Windows/macOS FOSS app counts. A PWA on a phone is not a separate native mobile app.

tools/beszel.note: The browser connects to a Beszel hub. Monitored hosts run a separate agent. A Web label is not a claim that the hub or agent runs on a phone.

tools/forgejo.note: Use the browser interface of a Forgejo server. Mobile browsers do not run the server; Git clients are a separate tool choice.

tools/freshrss.note: FreshRSS documents a responsive browser interface.
tools/freshrss.details: Its API-compatible native feed-reader apps are separate projects with their own source, licenses and features; they are not listed as native FreshRSS platforms.

tools/grafana.note: Grafana dashboards run in a browser connected to a Grafana server. Server packaging and plugins have separate requirements; this does not assert a native phone client.

tools/homepage.note: This is the web dashboard served by a Homepage installation, not a native app for each browser operating system.

tools/lubelogger.note: LubeLogger is web-based. Its Windows standalone executable hosts the service, not a separate native phone app.

tools/omni-tools.note: Self-hosted web utilities used through a browser. This does not imply native phone apps or identical behavior for every browser file format.

tools/paperless-ngx.note: The project provides a browser document-management interface.
tools/paperless-ngx.details: Third-party mobile clients are separate projects; the document server does not run on your phone merely because a client exists.

tools/penpot.note: The design editor runs in a browser against a hosted or self-hosted service. This is not a native iOS/Android app claim or a promise of full phone editing.

server.label: a self-hosted Plausible Community Edition server

tools/plausible.note: Plausible has a browser analytics dashboard. Self-hosted Community Edition versus the hosted service has separate setup and feature scope; this is not a native phone app.

tools/privacyidea.note: This is the management web UI for the authentication server.
tools/privacyidea.details: Token/authenticator apps and system integrations are separate projects; do not label them as the server running on iOS or Android.

tools/radicale.details: Its browser page is a limited management interface, not a full calendar/contact app. Compatible clients on phones/desktops are separate projects.

tools/umami.note: The analytics dashboard is a browser application. The analytics server, tracking script and hosted service have different roles; this is not a native phone client.

tools/uptime-kuma.note: The monitoring dashboard is used in a browser; the service must run elsewhere or on a supported host. No native phone app is asserted.

tools/vaultwarden.note: Vaultwarden is an independent server with a web vault, not the official Bitwarden mobile/desktop project.
tools/vaultwarden.details: Compatible Bitwarden clients have separate sources/licenses/releases. The project says to report Vaultwarden issues to its own maintainers, not Bitwarden support.

tools/victoriametrics.note: VMUI is a browser interface to a VictoriaMetrics server. This does not assert a native mobile client or that the database service runs on the phone.

tools/vikunja.note: The task interface is browser-based. Server installation targets and any third-party mobile clients are separate compatibility questions.

tools/pi-hole.note: This is the browser administration interface for a Pi-hole host. The phone is not running the DNS service merely because it opens the dashboard.

tools/adguard-home.note: AdGuard Home is the self-hosted DNS service, not the separate AdGuard Android/iOS content-blocking apps.
tools/adguard-home.details: Browser administration does not make a phone a supported server host.

tools/caddy.note: These are server host targets, not graphical desktop clients or native phone apps. Hosting and exposing a service requires a separate configuration and security plan.

tools/postgresql.note: Official download choices include these host platforms. PostgreSQL is a database server, not a native iPhone/Android graphical app. Optional database GUIs and remote clients are separate projects.

tools/percona-server.note: The official repository installation documentation covers Debian/Ubuntu and RHEL families. This is a server-host statement, not a mobile or desktop GUI client claim.

tools/ledger.note: The owning build documentation covers Linux and macOS workflows. A source reference to Windows/Python output is not enough to claim a normal supported Windows distribution. Other clients and wrappers are separate projects.

platforms.name: Android
platforms.kind: Firefox browser extension, not a standalone app

tools/ublock-origin.note: uBlock Origin documents Firefox desktop and Android support. Chrome removed the Manifest V2 listing on August 31, 2026; do not confuse uBlock Origin Lite with this project or promise Safari/iOS support.

tools/debian.note: Debian is an operating system, not an app for Windows, macOS, Android or iOS. Match the supported architecture and installation image to your hardware; the ports page distinguishes release architectures and other ports.

tools/fedora.note: Fedora Workstation is an operating system, not an app-platform download. Check the current edition, architecture and hardware requirements before choosing an image.

tools/freebsd.note: FreeBSD is an operating system. Its platform list distinguishes support tiers; a port existing is not identical support for every architecture or device. It is not an iPhone or Android replacement.

tools/kali-linux.note: Kali offers distinct installation, VM and other deployment routes. Match the route and hardware to the owning instructions. Its NetHunter phone offerings are device-specific separate installation paths, not evidence Kali replaces iOS or runs natively on every Android phone.

tools/linux-mint.note: Linux Mint is a desktop operating system. Choose its supported edition and image for compatible hardware, not an Android/iOS app or a Windows/macOS application.

tools/nixos.note: NixOS is the Linux operating system; Nix the package manager is a related but different install choice. Installing Nix on macOS does not mean macOS is running NixOS. Match the NixOS image and architecture to the machine.

tools/opensuse.note: openSUSE has different operating-system editions and install images. Choose the edition, architecture and hardware requirements explicitly; do not treat the OS as a Windows/macOS or phone app.

tools/pop-os.note: Pop!_OS is a desktop operating system. Choose the appropriate current image and compatible hardware using the official requirements, not a phone-app platform badge.

tools/ubuntu.note: Ubuntu Desktop is an operating system, not an application for the other desktop or phone OSes. The official image and hardware requirements apply to the specific edition and architecture.

tools/opnsense.note: OPNsense is a firewall/router operating system for supported hardware. Its web administration interface is not the OS running on your phone. Confirm hardware, network layout and recovery access before any installation or router cutover.

tools/grapheneos.note: Match the exact supported model/variant, unlock eligibility, maintained status and firmware-support lifetime. This replaces the OS on compatible Android hardware; it is not an Android app or an iPhone OS replacement. Installation can erase all phone data.

tools/calyxos.note: Match the exact supported model/variant, unlock eligibility, maintained status and firmware-support lifetime. This replaces the OS on compatible Android hardware; it is not an Android app or an iPhone OS replacement. Installation can erase all phone data.

tools/lineageos.note: Match the exact supported model/variant, unlock eligibility, maintained status and firmware-support lifetime. This replaces the OS on compatible Android hardware; it is not an Android app or an iPhone OS replacement. Installation can erase all phone data.

tools/parrot.note: Parrot OS is an operating system for AMD64 or ARM64 hardware and VMs, with WSL and Docker images; it is not an app for Windows, macOS, Android or iOS. Match the edition and architecture to your machine: the Security edition asks for 4 GB RAM minimum and 40 GB storage.

tools/almalinux.note: AlmaLinux OS is an operating system for x86_64 (including v2), aarch64, ppc64le and s390x, with live, cloud, container, Raspberry Pi and WSL images; it is not an app for another platform. Choose the 10 or 9 branch and the right architecture.

tools/tails.note: Tails runs live from a USB stick on PC or Mac hardware; it is not an app install and, per the project's install page, does not work on smartphones or tablets.

tools/qubes.note: Qubes OS needs 64-bit x86 hardware with VT-x/EPT and VT-d (or AMD equivalents): minimum 6 GB RAM and 32 GB storage, 16 GB RAM, SSD and Intel graphics recommended. Consult the HCL before choosing hardware.

tools/blackarch.note: BlackArch is a 64-bit Arch-based distribution, or a repository layer on an existing Arch install; it is not an app for another platform. The project recommends the netinstall or slim ISO over the full ISO.

tools/omarchy.note: Omarchy is an installable operating system: x86 and ARM64 ISOs plus a native Apple Silicon installer, with preliminary support for specific ARM hardware named on the site. It is not an app for another platform.

tools/technitium.note: Cross-platform .NET server administered through its web console on port 5380; free port 53 from any existing resolver first.

clients.name: Linux
clients.kind: Self-hosted server (omnibus Docker image or hub-and-spoke collectors)

tools/scrutiny.note: Collectors need device access (SYS_RAWIO, drive devices) to read S.M.A.R.T. data; remote machines report to one web server.

tools/cryptpad.note: Requires two separate domains (main and sandbox origin) served over HTTPS before browsers will load pads correctly.

tools/ollama.note: Native installers for the three desktop platforms plus a Docker image; serves a local API on port 11434 with no browser UI of its own. Match model size to your RAM/VRAM before pulling.

server.label: a copyparty server (a single file is enough)

platforms.name: Linux
platforms.kind: Single-file Python server (also PyPI and Docker)

tools/copyparty.note: Runs anywhere Python 3 does; web UI on port 3923 by default. Shares are reachable by anyone who can reach the port until you add accounts.

tools/warpgate.note: SSH on port 2222 and the web admin/HTTPS on 8888 by default; keep the admin UI on a trusted network.

platforms.name: Linux
platforms.kind: Official Docker image (compose is the documented route)

tools/mealie.note: Distributed as a Docker image (compose is the documented route); the web app works in any modern browser including phones. No native desktop or mobile apps.
